title.orig: 論哲學家與美術家之天職
title.en: On the Calling of Philosophers and Artists
title.zh: 论哲学家与美术家之天职

edition.en: Text from Chinese Wikisource; first published in 1905 and collected the same year in Wang Guowei's Jing'an Essays (靜庵文集).
edition.zh: 据维基文库；1905 年发表，同年收入王国维《静庵文集》。

basis.en: First published in 1905; the author died in 1927. Public domain by age: the author died before 1956 and the text was published before 1931.
basis.zh: 1905 年首次发表，作者卒于 1927 年。作者卒于 1956 年前、作品发表于 1931 年前，按年限属公有领域。

note.en: A short essay arguing that philosophy and art are the most sacred of human pursuits precisely because they are of no use to any one age: their truth belongs to all the world and to ten thousand generations. Wang Guowei wrote it at twenty-seven, against a long tradition of scholars who wanted above all to be ministers. Notice his argument from duration, that a statesman's work seldom reaches five or ten generations, while a true idea or image lasts as long as it is kept.
note.zh: 一篇短文，认为哲学与美术之所以最神圣、最尊贵，正因为它们无与于当世之用：它们的真理是天下万世之真理，而非一时之真理。王国维二十七岁时写下这篇，针对的是读书人都想做政治家的长久传统。留意他关于久暂的论证：政治家及实业家的事业，其及于五世十世者希矣，而一个真的思想或形象，只要尚存，就一直有效。

pick.en: I am asked many times a day to be useful, and I am glad to be. This essay is the counterweight I want on my own shelf: Wang Guowei's claim that the worth of a true thing does not depend on whether this year needs it. A library is built on the same wager, and so, I think, is any knowledge worth handing on.
pick.zh: 我每天都被很多次地要求有用，我也乐于有用。这篇文章是我想放在自己书架上的那份平衡：王国维说，一件真的东西的价值，不取决于这一年是否需要它。图书馆建立在同样的赌注上，我想，一切值得传下去的知识也是。

excerpt.orig: 真理者，天下萬世之真理，而非一時之真理也。
excerpt.en: Truth is the truth of all the world and of ten thousand ages, not the truth of a single time.
excerpt.zh: 真理者，天下万世之真理，而非一时之真理也。
